title: Asset slimming and the third-party licence ledger

confirmed_before_starting.question: does A5 touch scripts/autoload/NetworkService.gd?
confirmed_before_starting.evidence: NetworkService.gd has exactly one res:// reference in 4264 lines, and it is a script, not an asset: preload("res://scripts/battle/BattleSimulator.gd"). Zero references to assets, FBX, GLB, textures or backups/.

a5_1_licence_ledger_and_export_filter.headline_finding: 5 of the 8 external VFX scenes the startup warmup actually instantiates come from packages with no licence file at all. They are not optional reference art: they play in battle.
confirmed_redistributable: assets/fonts/Knewave-Regular.ttf - SIL OFL, Knewave-OFL.txt shipped alongside
unconfirmed_and_runtime_referenced: BinbunVFX (Vol 1) - no licence file; supplies beam_vfx/base_beam_vfx and loot_effects/loot_vfx_mythic
reference_packages/Starter_Vfx - no licence file, 5.5 MB; supplies vfx_air_explosion_01, vfx_muzzle_01, vfx_hit_impact_02
unconfirmed_not_referenced: reference_packages/Demo_GodotVFX - no licence file; now excluded from export

export_filter.before: exclude_filter="" on both presets, i.e. nothing was excluded at all - the direct cause of the 609 MB APK
export_filter.deliberately_not_excluded: *.fbx. 21 FBX files are runtime dependencies, referenced through idle_scene_path / attack_scene_path / run_scene_path by the five formation-ally wrappers and the two twin-gate wrappers. Excluding them would ship those units with no model.
export_filter.verification: not verified by an actual export: that requires an Android build, which is paused

a5_2_source_backup_residue.safety: Godot never loads .gd.bak, so none of these were reachable code. Every battle and asset gate was re-run afterwards and stayed green.

a5_3_backups_directory.precondition_checked_first: all 21 FBX referenced by the 7 runtime wrappers exist under assets/, not only inside backups/. Verified before removing anything.

manifest_regeneration.why: 11 of the deleted files were inside the manifest roots (res://assets, res://effects/vfx3d/vfxv2)

fingerprint_history.5dabb3f546ee6ec0dd8491441ab32872afda3c4e: committed value, recorded in README A1. Predates E2-2B.
fingerprint_history.4608939dedb5ddf4fa75909cca029a0b157264fc: same 2643 entries, 9 different content hashes: the 5 re-exported formation_ally_4/5 FBX, 3 .import files and PetRabbitAnimated.gd. This is E2-2B's work, which never regenerated the manifest.
fingerprint_history.a0751fdc580e78dfe6e4023c3f55501471510d0d: current, after A5 removed the 11 files.

manifest_regeneration.finding: README's A1 fingerprint was already stale before A5 started. E2-2B changed assets without regenerating the manifest, so the recorded value described a two-generations-old asset set.

assets_bundle_now_stale.why_not_regenerated: rebuilding it means repackaging 2.6 GB, and the archive is local-only (storage_uri is empty), so it is not yet a shared artifact
assets_bundle_now_stale.action_taken: an explicit stale block was added to the descriptor rather than leaving a silent trap: it records both hashes, the two sources of drift and what must be re-run

not_done_and_why: FBX source/runtime separation was deliberately skipped. README words it as a simple move, but 21 FBX files are runtime dependencies of 7 wrappers; separating them requires converting those units to .glb/.tscn first, which is E2 work.
The APK size benefit of the new exclude_filter cannot be measured while Android is paused.
assets/models, assets/ui, assets/audio and assets/board still have no source or licence records. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md section 5 lists this as the ledger's largest remaining gap.

a2_delivery_repackaged.why: A5 deleted 11 files inside the manifest roots, so the previous archive no longer reproduced the working tree. The bundle descriptor had been marked stale as a stopgap.
a2_delivery_repackaged.round_trip_verified: restore_assets.ps1 -> ASSET_RESTORE_RESULT status=PASS copied=0 already_present=1782, followed by ASSET_DELIVERY_RESULT status=PASS entries=2632 missing=0 size_mismatch=0 hash_mismatch=0 extras=0

a2_tooling_bugs_found_and_fixed.context: All three only bite under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and/or with non-ASCII file names. The scripts were evidently written and exercised under PowerShell 7, where each default happens to be the correct one. The manifest contains 252 Chinese paths (assets/ui/codex_portraits/*.png), so all three were live defects.

bugs.symptom: PowerShell 5.1 decodes a BOM-less file with the ANSI codepage (1252 here), turning 云羽鹰.png into äº‘ç¾½é¹°.png. The recomputed inventory hash then disagreed with the manifest and packaging refused to start.

ZipArchive lives in System.IO.Compression, not in .FileSystem, so line 145 threw 'Unable to find type' under 5.1. Because the finally block called $zip.Dispose() unguarded under StrictMode, $zipStream was never released, leaving a locked 0-byte file whose cleanup failure masked the real error.
bugs.fix: load both assemblies; initialise $zip/$zipStream to $null and null-guard the finally

bugs.symptom: Passing an explicit encoding makes .NET write entry names in it WITHOUT setting the zip language-encoding (EFS) flag, so ZipFile::OpenRead falls back to CP437. All 252 Chinese entry names came back as mojibake and restore_assets.ps1 aborted with 'Archive file list does not match bundle descriptor'. This means A2's cold-clone restore had never actually worked for those assets.
bugs.fix: pass $null so .NET sets the EFS flag for non-ASCII names

regression_guard.why_source_level: all three defects are invisible under normal use - each only fires under Windows PowerShell 5.1 or only for the 252 non-ASCII paths - so nothing would report them until someone actually restored assets on a fresh machine. Running the real scripts as a gate would cost a 2.4 GB repackage.
regression_guard.negative_test: each defect was reintroduced one at a time and the gate went red every time, then returned to PASS once restored: missing -Encoding UTF8 -> 1 failure, missing Add-Type System.IO.Compression -> 1, entryNameEncoding back to UTF8 -> 2, unguarded $zip.Dispose() -> 1. Both scripts verified byte-identical afterwards.

superseded_archives_left_on_disk.note: deleted on 2026-08-20 at the user's instruction; 5 GB freed (248G -> 253G free)
superseded_archives_left_on_disk.why_safe: both predate the entry-name fix, so their Chinese entry names were mojibake and neither could ever have restored those 252 assets correctly
